Theme

Latin word

quandō

indefinite adverb: sī quandō, if ever

ever (after sī, nisi, nē, num); when?

In this lexicon

  • ever

    also used · classical · Mor. 67: sī quandō vacuum casula pluviaeve tenēbant; Catull. 84.1: sī quandō commoda vellet dīcere

  • when

    the recommended word · classical · Ter. Eun. 697: Quandō? — Hodiē.; Cic. Fam. 16.18.3: tē quandō exspectēmus fac ut sciam; Traupman 406

Notes

  1. 1quandō: long final o (Lewis & Short leaves it unmarked). De Vaan 507, s.v. quī, gives the final vowel long; Festus records an older quandōd (Lewis & Short s.v. quando). Shortened to quando in later verse. As in aliquandō (see “ever”); the libellī write quandō.

Examples

  • Quandō? — Hodiē. — Quam dūdum? — Modo.

    When? — Today. — How long ago? — Just now.Ter. Eun. 697

    In the entry for when

  • crās tē vīctūrum, crās dīcis, Postume, semper: dīc mihi, crās istud, Postume, quandō venit?

    Tomorrow you will live, you always say, Postumus, tomorrow: tell me, Postumus, when does that tomorrow come?Mart. 5.58.1–2

    In the entry for when

  • tē quandō exspectēmus fac ut sciam. cūrā tē dīligenter. valē.

    Let me know when we should expect you. Look after yourself. Goodbye.Cic. Fam. 16.18.3

    In the entry for when

  • Quandō vīs venī, parāta rēs erit. — Properā modo.

    Come when you like, it will be ready. — Just hurry.Plaut. Men. 215–215b
